I would keep it simple and stable. In Quzhou County, I would stay with the wheat-maize rotation on my land because I know it fits the climate, the soils, the water conditions, and the way I can manage work through the year. I would carry my winter wheat through harvest, then plant summer maize right after. I would not spread myself across many crops, because with my situation I would rather protect yield and reduce risk than chase something uncertain. For wheat, I would focus on topdressing nitrogen, a few irrigations at key stages, and basic disease and pest control. After wheat harvest, I would move fast into maize, use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer balanced, irrigate when needed, and control weeds and borers with a small number of pesticide sprays. I am assuming I am planning for 20 mu of land and using the same land for the wheat-maize double-cropping cycle.
